files.START_HERE.md:
# Start Here

Read this before anything else. It takes about ten minutes and it assumes you have never opened a terminal in your life.

If you get stuck, jump to [When something goes wrong](#when-something-goes-wrong) at the bottom. Every common error is listed there with the fix.

---

## What you need

Python 3.11 or newer. That is the whole list.

### Do you already have it?

Open a terminal (next section explains how), then type this and press Enter.

**Mac:**
```
python3 --version
```

**Windows:**
```
python --version
```

If it prints `Python 3.11` or higher, you are set. Skip to Step 1.

If it prints a lower number, or says the command was not found, install Python from [python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/). Take the big yellow download button.

> **Mac users:** older Macs shipped with Python 2.7, which will not work here. If your version starts with `2`, install a new one from python.org. The new one sits alongside the old one and does not break anything.

> **Windows users:** during install, tick the box that says **Add Python to PATH** on the first screen. It is easy to miss and it causes most Windows problems later.

---

## How to open a terminal

**Mac:** press `Command` + `Space`, type `Terminal`, press Enter.

**Windows:** press the `Windows` key, type `PowerShell`, press Enter.

A window opens with some text and a blinking cursor. That is a terminal. You type a command, press Enter, and it does the thing. It cannot break your computer by being open.

---

## Step 1: Install the course

Find the `code-skool` folder you unzipped.

**Mac:** right click (or hold Control and click) on `install-mac.command`, choose **Open**, then click **Open** again in the box that appears.

> Right click and choose Open. Do not double click it. macOS blocks files downloaded from the internet and double clicking shows "cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer" with no way forward. Right click and Open gives you the button that lets it through. You only have to do this once.

**Windows:** double click `install-windows.bat`. If a blue box says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.

It runs for a minute or two and shows a progress bar. When it finishes it prints three lines. **Leave that window open**, you are about to use them.

---

## Step 2: Point your terminal at the course folder

This is the step that stops most people. There is a trick that makes it easy.

Open a **new** terminal window. Type `cd` and then a space. **Do not press Enter yet.**

```
cd 
```

Now drag the `code-skool` folder from Finder (or File Explorer) and drop it onto the terminal window. Let go. It pastes the full path for you, so you never have to type it or know what it is.

Press Enter.

> The installer printed this exact line for you in Step 1. Copying that line works just as well.

**How to know it worked:** type `ls` on Mac or `dir` on Windows and press Enter. You should see `README.md`, `weeks`, `work`, and `projects` listed. If you do not, you are in the wrong folder. Try the drag trick again.

---

## Step 3: Turn the course on

**Mac:**
```
source .venv/bin/activate
```

**Windows:**
```
.venv\Scripts\activate
```

**How to know it worked:** your prompt now starts with `(.venv)`. If you do not see that, it did not work.

**What this actually does:** the installer built a private, self contained Python setup inside the course folder. Activating points this terminal window at that private setup instead of the rest of your computer. It means the course cannot interfere with anything else you have installed, and nothing else can break the course.

**You do this every time you open a new terminal window to work on the course.** Close the terminal, come back tomorrow, and you run this line again first. Forgetting it is the single most common cause of errors.

---

## Step 4: Open the course

```
python -m code_skool
```

You should see the CODE SKOOL screen with your progress on it. That is the course itself, running on your machine.

---

## Step 5: Read your first lesson

```
cat weeks/week-01/README.md
```

`cat` means "show me what is in this file". The lesson prints right there in the terminal.

If reading in the terminal is uncomfortable, that same file is a normal file on your computer. Open `weeks/week-01/README.md` in any text editor and read it there. TextEdit, Notepad, VS Code, anything.

---

## Step 6: Do your first exercise

Open the exercise file:

**Mac:**
```
open work/week-01/ex01_variable_explorer.py
```

**Windows:**
```
start work\week-01\ex01_variable_explorer.py
```

Inside you will find comments starting with `TODO`. Each one tells you what to write. Write your code under each TODO, then save the file.

Run it:

```
python work/week-01/ex01_variable_explorer.py
```

Whatever your code prints shows up in the terminal. If you got an error, read the last line of it. It usually names the problem and the line number.

Stuck? The answers are right here:

```
cat weeks/week-01/solutions.md
```

Looking at the solution is not cheating. Type it out yourself instead of copying and pasting, and you will still learn it.

When `ex01` works, move to `ex02`, and keep going. After the exercises comes the week's mini project.

---

## That is the whole loop

**Read** the lesson. **Write** code in the exercise file. **Run** it. Repeat.

Six weeks, one week at a time. Nothing is graded, nothing is submitted, there is no account and no deadline. You can take six weeks or six months.

---

## When something goes wrong

| What you see | What it means | The fix |
|---|---|---|
| `command not found: python` | You skipped activation | Do Step 3 again |
| `No module named code_skool` | Not activated, or wrong folder | Do Step 2, then Step 3 |
| `can't open file ... No such file or directory` | Your terminal is in the wrong folder | Do Step 2. Check with `ls` or `dir` |
| `cannot be opened because it is from an unidentified developer` | macOS is blocking the installer | Right click the file and choose Open |
| `Windows protected your PC` | Windows is blocking the installer | Click More info, then Run anyway |
| `permission denied` on the installer | The file is not marked runnable | Run `chmod +x install-mac.command` then try again |
| `python: command not found` on Mac even after activating | Python was never installed | Install from python.org, then run the installer again |
| Your prompt has no `(.venv)` | Activation did not take | Check you are in the course folder first, then Step 3 |

### Starting completely over

Nothing here is precious. Delete the `.venv` folder inside `code-skool` and run the installer again. Your work in `work/` is untouched.

---

## What this course does not do

It does not connect to the internet. It does not create an account. It does not send anything anywhere. There is no API key to buy and nothing to subscribe to.

Once these files are on your computer, the whole course works with your wifi switched off. That is on purpose.

# CODE Skool: Learn to Code with Python

*Every expert was once a beginner.*

A 6-week course that teaches programming from scratch. No experience required.

---

## Setup (one time)

**Mac:** Double-click `install-mac.command`
**Windows:** Double-click `install-windows.bat`

That's it. The installer checks your Python version, creates a virtual environment, and installs everything you need.

> **Troubleshooting:** If the installer won't open on Mac, right-click it and choose "Open". On Windows, right-click and "Run as administrator". You need Python 3.11+ from [python.org](https://www.python.org/downloads/).

---

## How This Works

Every day you do three things:

1. **Read** the lesson
2. **Write** code in the exercise file
3. **Run** it

That's it.

---

## Getting Started

Open a terminal and run:

```bash
cd /path/to/code-skool
source .venv/bin/activate       # Mac/Linux
# .venv\Scripts\activate.bat    # Windows
```

Read the Week 1 lesson:

```bash
cat weeks/week-01/README.md
```

Open your first exercise file in any text editor (VS Code, Thonny, or even TextEdit):

```bash
open work/week-01/ex01_variable_explorer.py     # Mac
# Or just open the file from your editor
```

Write your code in the file, then run it:

```bash
python work/week-01/ex01_variable_explorer.py
```

When it works, move to `ex02_mad_libs.py`. Repeat for the rest of the exercises, then build the mini-project.

---

## What's Where

```
work/           Your code goes here (edit these files)
weeks/          Lessons, exercise descriptions, solutions (read these)
projects/       Three capstone projects you'll build
reference/      Look things up when you're stuck
course-info/    Course overview and pacing schedules
code/           Internal package (you don't need to touch this)
```

---

## Weekly Routine

Each week has a set of exercises and 1 mini-project:

```bash
# 1. Read the lesson
cat weeks/week-01/README.md

# 2. Read the exercise descriptions (for examples and details)
cat weeks/week-01/exercises.md

# 3. Open an exercise file and write your code
python work/week-01/ex01_variable_explorer.py

# 4. When done, check your work against the solutions
cat weeks/week-01/solutions.md

# 5. Grade yourself
cat weeks/week-01/rubric.md
```

---

## Course Map

| Week | Topic | Project |
|------|-------|---------|
| 1 | Variables & Data Types | none |
| 2 | Control Flow (if/else) | Calculator |
| 3 | Loops (for/while) | none |
| 4 | Functions | Number Guessing Game |
| 5 | Data Structures (lists, dicts) | none |
| 6 | Files & Integration | Contact Manager |

---

## Stuck?

```bash
cat reference/debugging.md          # Common errors and how to fix them
cat reference/glossary.md           # What does this word mean?
cat reference/cheat-sheet.md        # Quick syntax reference
cat reference/variables-and-types.md  # Deep dive on variables
cat reference/control-flow.md       # Deep dive on if/elif/else
cat reference/loops.md              # Deep dive on loops
cat reference/functions.md          # Deep dive on functions
cat reference/data-structures.md    # Deep dive on lists, dicts, sets
cat reference/files-io.md           # Deep dive on file I/O
```

---

## Pacing

- **6-week standard** (6-8 hrs/week): `cat course-info/track-6-week.md`
- **4-week intensive** (12-15 hrs/week): `cat course-info/track-4-week.md`
- **Course philosophy and objectives**: `cat course-info/overview.md`

---

## What Comes Next?

```
CODE Skool (you are here) --> PY Skool --> AI Skool
  Fundamentals                Intermediate    Advanced
  Variables, loops,           Classes,        AI agents,
  functions, data             decorators,     LLMs, tools,
  structures                  async, types    production systems
```

#!/bin/bash
#
# CODE Skool: Installer
# Double-click this file to set up the course.
#
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
COURSE_DIR="$(pwd)"

# --- Theme: Neon Yellow ---
BOLD="\033[1m"
RESET="\033[0m"
NEON="\033[93m"
GREY="\033[90m"
WHITE="\033[97m"
RED="\033[91m"

# Two-tone ASCII art: bold bright yellow blocks, bright yellow shadows
colorize() {
    local b=$'\033[1;93m'
    local s=$'\033[93m'
    local r=$'\033[0m'
    sed "s/█/${b}█/g; s/╔/${s}╔/g; s/═/${s}═/g; s/╗/${s}╗/g; s/╚/${s}╚/g; s/╝/${s}╝/g; s/║/${s}║/g; s/$/${r}/"
}

# --- Single Progress Bar (no labels, just bar + %) ---
CURRENT_PCT=0

draw_bar() {
    local pct=$1
    local width=40
    local filled=$((pct * width / 100))
    local empty=$((width - filled))
    local bar=""

    for ((i=0; i<filled; i++)); do bar+="\033[1;93m█"; done
    for ((i=0; i<empty; i++)); do bar+="\033[90m░"; done

    printf "\r  \033[93m[\033[0m${bar}\033[0m\033[93m]\033[0m \033[1;93m%3d%%\033[0m" "$pct"
}

run_step() {
    local target_pct=$1
    shift
    local cmd="$*"

    local tmpfile
    tmpfile=$(mktemp)
    eval "$cmd" > "$tmpfile" 2>&1 &
    local pid=$!

    local near_target=$((target_pct - 3))
    while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
        if [ $CURRENT_PCT -lt $near_target ]; then
            CURRENT_PCT=$((CURRENT_PCT + 1))
        fi
        draw_bar "$CURRENT_PCT"
        sleep 0.06
    done

    wait "$pid" || true

    CURRENT_PCT=$target_pct
    draw_bar "$CURRENT_PCT"
    rm -f "$tmpfile"
}

instant_step() {
    local target_pct=$1

    while [ $CURRENT_PCT -lt $target_pct ]; do
        CURRENT_PCT=$((CURRENT_PCT + 1))
        draw_bar "$CURRENT_PCT"
        sleep 0.02
    done
}

# --- Start ---
clear

echo ""
cat << 'LOGO' | colorize
     ██████╗ ██████╗ ██████╗ ███████╗
    ██╔════╝██╔═══██╗██╔══██╗██╔════╝
    ██║     ██║   ██║██║  ██║█████╗
    ██║     ██║   ██║██║  ██║██╔══╝
    ╚██████╗╚██████╔╝██████╔╝███████╗
     ╚═════╝ ╚═════╝ ╚═════╝ ╚══════╝
    ███████╗██╗  ██╗ ██████╗  ██████╗ ██╗
    ██╔════╝██║ ██╔╝██╔═══██╗██╔═══██╗██║
    ███████╗█████╔╝ ██║   ██║██║   ██║██║
    ╚════██║██╔═██╗ ██║   ██║██║   ██║██║
    ███████║██║  ██╗╚██████╔╝╚██████╔╝███████╗
    ╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝ ╚═════╝  ╚═════╝ ╚══════╝
LOGO
echo ""
echo -e "  ${GREY}Learn to Code with Python${RESET}"
echo -e "  ${NEON}\"Every expert was once a beginner.\"${RESET}"
echo ""

sleep 0.3

# ── Python check (0 → 10%) ────────────────────────────────────
instant_step 10

if ! command -v python3 &>/dev/null; then
    printf "\r%-80s\n" ""
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET}  ${GREY}python3 not found${RESET}"
    echo -e "  ${GREY}Install Python 3.11+ from ${NEON}https://python.org/downloads${RESET}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${GREY}Press Enter to close.${RESET}"
    read -r
    osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to close front window' 2>/dev/null &
    exit 1
fi

# Check Python version >= 3.11
PY_VERSION=$(python3 -c "import sys; print(f'{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}')")
PY_MAJOR=$(python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.version_info.major)")
PY_MINOR=$(python3 -c "import sys; print(sys.version_info.minor)")

if [ "$PY_MAJOR" -lt 3 ] || ([ "$PY_MAJOR" -eq 3 ] && [ "$PY_MINOR" -lt 11 ]); then
    printf "\r%-80s\n" ""
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET}  ${GREY}Python ${PY_VERSION} found, but 3.11+ is required${RESET}"
    echo -e "  ${GREY}Install Python 3.11+ from ${NEON}https://python.org/downloads${RESET}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${GREY}Press Enter to close.${RESET}"
    read -r
    osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to close front window' 2>/dev/null &
    exit 1
fi

# ── Create venv (10 → 30%) ────────────────────────────────────
if [ -d ".venv" ]; then
    instant_step 30
else
    run_step 30 "python3 -m venv .venv"
fi

source .venv/bin/activate

# ── Upgrade pip (30 → 50%) ────────────────────────────────────
run_step 50 "pip install --quiet --upgrade pip"

# ── Install package (50 → 85%) ────────────────────────────────
run_step 85 "pip install --quiet -e code/"

# ── Verify import (85 → 100%) ─────────────────────────────────
instant_step 95

if python3 -c "import code_skool" 2>/dev/null; then
    instant_step 100
else
    printf "\r%-80s\n" ""
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${RED}✗${RESET}  ${GREY}Installation failed. Try manually:${RESET}"
    echo -e "    ${NEON}python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e code/${RESET}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${GREY}Press Enter to close.${RESET}"
    read -r
    osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to close front window' 2>/dev/null &
    exit 1
fi

# Clear the progress bar line
printf "\r%-80s\r" ""
echo ""

sleep 0.3

cat << 'COMPLETE' | colorize
    ██████╗ ███████╗ █████╗ ██████╗ ██╗   ██╗
    ██╔══██╗██╔════╝██╔══██╗██╔══██╗╚██╗ ██╔╝
    ██████╔╝█████╗  ███████║██║  ██║ ╚████╔╝
    ██╔══██╗██╔══╝  ██╔══██║██║  ██║  ╚██╔╝
    ██║  ██║███████╗██║  ██║██████╔╝   ██║
    ╚═╝  ╚═╝╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝╚═════╝    ╚═╝
COMPLETE
echo ""
echo -e "  ${BOLD}${WHITE}Your course is ready.${RESET}"
echo ""
echo -e "  ${GREY}Open a new Terminal window and run:${RESET}"
echo ""
echo -e "    ${NEON}cd \"${COURSE_DIR}\"${RESET}"
echo -e "    ${NEON}source .venv/bin/activate${RESET}"
echo -e "    ${NEON}python -m code_skool${RESET}"
echo ""
echo -e "  ${GREY}Press Enter to close.${RESET}"
read -r
osascript -e 'tell application "Terminal" to close front window' 2>/dev/null &
exit 0

@echo off
rem
rem CODE Skool: Windows Installer
rem Double-click this file to set up the course.
rem
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
chcp 65001 >nul 2>&1
cd /d "%~dp0"
set "COURSE_DIR=%cd%"

rem --- Escape character for ANSI colors ---
for /f %%a in ('echo prompt $E ^| cmd') do set "ESC=%%a"

rem --- Theme: Neon Yellow ---
set "BOLD=%ESC%[1m"
set "RESET=%ESC%[0m"
set "NEON=%ESC%[93m"
set "GREY=%ESC%[90m"
set "WHITE=%ESC%[97m"
set "RED=%ESC%[91m"
set "BNEON=%ESC%[1;93m"

cls

echo.
echo %BNEON%     ██████╗ ██████╗ ██████╗ ███████╗%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ██╔%NEON%════╝%BNEON%██╔%NEON%═══%BNEON%██╗██╔%NEON%══%BNEON%██╗██╔%NEON%════╝%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ██║     ██║   ██║██║  ██║█████╗%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ██║     ██║   ██║██║  ██║██╔%NEON%══╝%RESET%
echo %NEON%    ╚%BNEON%██████╗%NEON%╚%BNEON%██████╔%NEON%╝%BNEON%██████╔%NEON%╝%BNEON%███████╗%RESET%
echo %NEON%     ╚═════╝ ╚═════╝ ╚═════╝ ╚══════╝%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ███████╗██╗  ██╗ ██████╗  ██████╗ ██╗%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ██╔%NEON%════╝%BNEON%██║ ██╔%NEON%╝%BNEON%██╔%NEON%═══%BNEON%██╗██╔%NEON%═══%BNEON%██╗██║%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ███████╗█████╔%NEON%╝ %BNEON%██║   ██║██║   ██║██║%RESET%
echo %NEON%    ╚════%BNEON%██║██╔%NEON%═%BNEON%██╗ ██║   ██║██║   ██║██║%RESET%
echo %BNEON%    ███████║██║  ██╗%NEON%╚%BNEON%██████╔%NEON%╝╚%BNEON%██████╔%NEON%╝%BNEON%███████╗%RESET%
echo %NEON%    ╚══════╝╚═╝  ╚═╝ ╚═════╝  ╚═════╝ ╚══════╝%RESET%
echo.
echo   %GREY%Learn to Code with Python%RESET%
echo   %NEON%"Every expert was once a beginner."%RESET%
echo.

timeout /t 1 /nobreak >nul

rem --- Step 1: Check for Python (0 -> 10%) ---
call :draw_bar 5
set "PYTHON_CMD="

where python >nul 2>&1
if !errorlevel! equ 0 (
    rem Verify it's real Python, not the Windows Store stub
    python --version >nul 2>&1
    if !errorlevel! equ 0 (
        set "PYTHON_CMD=python"
    )
)

if not defined PYTHON_CMD (
    where python3 >nul 2>&1
    if !errorlevel! equ 0 (
        set "PYTHON_CMD=python3"
    )
)

call :draw_bar 10

if not defined PYTHON_CMD (
    echo.
    echo.
    echo   %RED%X%RESET%  %GREY%Python not found%RESET%
    echo   %GREY%Install Python 3.11+ from %NEON%https://python.org/downloads%RESET%
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)

rem --- Check Python version >= 3.11 ---
for /f "tokens=*" %%v in ('%PYTHON_CMD% -c "import sys; print(f'{sys.version_info.major}.{sys.version_info.minor}')"') do set "PY_VERSION=%%v"
for /f "tokens=*" %%v in ('%PYTHON_CMD% -c "import sys; print(1 if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else 0)"') do set "PY_OK=%%v"

if "!PY_OK!" neq "1" (
    echo.
    echo.
    echo   %RED%X%RESET%  %GREY%Python !PY_VERSION! found, but 3.11+ is required%RESET%
    echo   %GREY%Install Python 3.11+ from %NEON%https://python.org/downloads%RESET%
    echo.
    pause
    exit /b 1
)

rem --- Step 2: Create venv (10 -> 30%) ---
if exist ".venv" (
    call :draw_bar 30
) else (
    call :draw_bar 15
    %PYTHON_CMD% -m venv .venv >nul 2>&1
    if !errorlevel! neq 0 (
        echo.
        echo.
        echo   %RED%X%RESET%  %GREY%Failed to create virtual environment.%RESET%
        echo.
        pause
        exit /b 1
    )
    call :draw_bar 30
)

call .venv\Scripts\activate.bat >nul 2>&1

rem --- Step 3: Upgrade pip (30 -> 50%) ---
call :draw_bar 35
%PYTHON_CMD% -m pip install --quiet --upgrade pip >nul 2>&1
call :draw_bar 50

rem --- Step 4: Install package (50 -> 85%) ---

```python
print(f"Value: {my_float}  |  Type: {type(my_float)}")
```

## Exercise 3 Solution: Tip Calculator

```python
# ============================================================

# Practice type conversion and math with formatted output
# ============================================================

print("=== TIP CALCULATOR ===\n")

# --- Get input from the user ---
# input() always returns a string, so we convert to the right type

# float() converts the string to a decimal number
bill_amount = float(input("Enter the bill amount: $"))

# We can use either int() or float() for the percentage
# int() is fine since most people use whole number percentages
tip_percentage = float(input("Enter the tip percentage: "))

# int() converts to a whole number (you can't have 2.5 people!)
num_people = int(input("How many people are splitting? "))

# --- Calculate the results ---

# Tip amount: bill times the percentage divided by 100
# (dividing by 100 converts a percentage like 18 into a decimal like 0.18)
tip_amount = bill_amount * tip_percentage / 100

# Total: the original bill plus the tip
total = bill_amount + tip_amount

# Per person: divide the total evenly among everyone
per_person = total / num_people

# --- Display the results ---
# :.2f means "format as a float with exactly 2 decimal places"
# This is perfect for money. We always want $9.50, not $9.5

print("\n--- Bill Summary ---")
print(f"Bill amount:    ${bill_amount:.2f}")
print(f"Tip ({tip_percentage:.0f}%):      ${tip_amount:.2f}")
print(f"Total:          ${total:.2f}")
print(f"Per person ({num_people}): ${per_person:.2f}")

# Bonus: show some extra info
print(f"\nEach person saves ${(bill_amount / num_people):.2f} on the bill alone")
print(f"and pays ${(tip_amount / num_people):.2f} toward the tip.")
```

## Exercise 4 Solution: Temperature Converter

```python
# ============================================================
# Exercise 4: Temperature Converter
# Practice math formulas, conditionals preview, and f-strings
# ============================================================

print("=== TEMPERATURE CONVERTER ===\n")

# --- Ask which conversion direction ---
print("1. Fahrenheit to Celsius")
print("2. Celsius to Fahrenheit")
choice = input("Choose (1 or 2): ")

# --- Get the temperature value ---
# We convert to float so it can handle decimals like 98.6
temp = float(input("Enter the temperature: "))

# --- Perform the conversion ---
# We check the user's choice to decide which formula to use

if choice == "1":
    # Fahrenheit to Celsius formula: C = (F - 32) * 5/9
    result = (temp - 32) * 5 / 9
    # :.1f means format with 1 decimal place
    print(f"\n{temp:.1f}\u00b0F = {result:.1f}\u00b0C")

    # Add a comment about the temperature (using Celsius result)
    if result <= 0:
        print("Brr! That's freezing cold! Water turns to ice at this temperature.")
    elif result <= 15:
        print("That's quite chilly. Grab a jacket!")
    elif result <= 25:
        print("That's a comfortable room temperature!")
    elif result <= 35:
        print("Nice and warm! Great weather for the beach.")
    else:
        print("That's extremely hot! Stay hydrated!")

elif choice == "2":
    # Celsius to Fahrenheit formula: F = (C * 9/5) + 32
    result = (temp * 9 / 5) + 32
    print(f"\n{temp:.1f}\u00b0C = {result:.1f}\u00b0F")

    # Add a comment about the temperature (using Celsius input)
    if temp <= 0:
        print("Brr! That's freezing cold! Water turns to ice at this temperature.")
    elif temp <= 15:
        print("That's quite chilly. Grab a jacket!")
    elif temp <= 25:
        print("That's a comfortable room temperature!")
    elif temp <= 35:
        print("Nice and warm! Great weather for the beach.")
    else:
        print("That's extremely hot! Stay hydrated!")

else:
    # If the user didn't type 1 or 2

# --- Bonus: show some reference points ---
print("\n--- Reference Temperatures ---")

print(f"Room temp:     20\u00b0C / 68\u00b0F")
print(f"Body temp:     37\u00b0C / 98.6\u00b0F")
print(f"Water boils:   100\u00b0C / 212\u00b0F")
```

## Exercise 5 Solution: String Explorer

```python
# ============================================================
# Exercise 5: String Explorer
# Practice string methods, slicing, and len()
# ============================================================

print("=== STRING EXPLORER ===\n")

# --- Get the user's name ---
name = input("Enter your full name: ")

# --- Demonstrate string operations ---
print(f"\n--- String Explorer Results ---")

# Original name, just as they typed it
print(f"Original:       {name}")

# .upper() converts every letter to UPPERCASE
print(f"Uppercase:      {name.upper()}")

# .lower() converts every letter to lowercase
print(f"Lowercase:      {name.lower()}")

# len() counts the number of characters (including spaces!)
print(f"Length:         {len(name)} characters")

# Slicing with [::-1] reverses a string
# The -1 means "step backwards through the string"
reversed_name = name[::-1]
print(f"Reversed:       {reversed_name}")

# Indexing: [0] gets the first character, [-1] gets the last
# Remember: Python counts from 0, not 1!
print(f"First letter:   {name[0]}")
print(f"Last letter:    {name[-1]}")

# .replace() swaps one substring for another
print(f"With dashes:    {name.replace(' ', '-')}")

# The * operator repeats a string
print(f"Repeated (x3):  {name * 3}")

# Check if the name starts with a vowel
# We use .upper() so it works whether they typed uppercase or lowercase
first_letter = name[0].upper()
# The "in" keyword checks if something is inside a collection
is_vowel = first_letter in "AEIOU"
# We print "Yes" or "No" based on the True/False value
print(f"Starts with vowel: {'Yes' if is_vowel else 'No'}")

# --- Bonus operations ---
print(f"\n--- Bonus ---")

# .title() capitalizes the first letter of each word
print(f"Title case:     {name.title()}")

# .count() counts how many times a character appears
print(f"Letter 'a' count: {name.lower().count('a')}")

# .startswith() and .endswith() check the beginning/end
print(f"Starts with 'A': {name.startswith('A')}")

# .strip() removes leading/trailing whitespace
print(f"Stripped:       '{name.strip()}'")

# Number of words (split by spaces)
words = name.split()
print(f"Number of words: {len(words)}")

# Each word on its own line
for i, word in enumerate(words):
    print(f"  Word {i + 1}: {word}")
```

## Mini-Project Solution: Personal Profile Card

```python
# ============================================================
# Mini-Project: Personal Profile Card
# Combines variables, input, type conversion, f-strings,
# math, and string operations into one complete program
# ============================================================

# --- Step 1: Collect information from the user ---

print("=== PROFILE CARD GENERATOR ===\n")

# input() gets text from the user and stores it in a variable
name = input("Enter your full name: ")
age_input = input("Enter your age: ")
city = input("Enter your city: ")
color = input("Enter your favorite color: ")
hobby = input("Enter your hobby or interest: ")

# --- Step 2: Convert types and calculate derived values ---

# Convert age from string to integer so we can do math with it
age = int(age_input)

# Calculate approximate birth year
# We use 2026 as the current year
current_year = 2026
birth_year = current_year - age

# Calculate approximate days alive
# (not exact, doesn't account for leap years, but close enough!)
days_alive = age * 365

# Generate a username from the first 3 letters of the name + birth year
# We use min(3, len(name)) in case the name is shorter than 3 characters
# .replace(" ", "") removes spaces so "Al S" becomes "AlS", not "Al "
name_no_spaces = name.replace(" ", "")
username_prefix = name_no_spaces[:min(3, len(name_no_spaces))]
username = f"{username_prefix}{birth_year}"

# Count characters in the name
name_length = len(name)

# Create reversed name using string slicing
# [::-1] means "start at the end, go backwards"
reversed_name = name[::-1]

# --- Step 3: Build the profile card ---

# Define the card width
width = 44

# Build horizontal border lines
# "=" * 42 creates a string of 42 equal signs
top_border = "+" + "=" * (width - 2) + "+"
mid_border = "+" + "-" * (width - 2) + "+"
bot_border = "+" + "=" * (width - 2) + "+"

# A blank line inside the card
blank_line = "|" + " " * (width - 2) + "|"

# Helper: pad a line to fit inside the card borders
# This function takes some text and puts it inside | ... |
# with the right amount of spaces to reach the border
def card_line(text):
    # (width - 4) because we need space for "|  " on the left and " |" on the right
    # ljust() pads the string with spaces on the right to reach a certain length
    inner = text.ljust(width - 4)
    return f"|  {inner}|"

# --- Step 4: Print the card ---

print()  # blank line before the card

# Title section
print(top_border)
title = "PERSONAL PROFILE CARD"
# .center() centers the text within the given width
print("|" + title.center(width - 2) + "|")
print(top_border)

# Blank line for spacing
print(blank_line)

# Personal information
print(card_line(f"Name:       {name}"))
print(card_line(f"Username:   {username}"))
print(card_line(f"Age:        {age} years old"))
print(card_line(f"Birth Year: {birth_year} (approximately)"))
print(card_line(f"Days Alive: ~{days_alive:,} days"))
print(card_line(f"City:       {city}"))
print(card_line(f"Color:      {color}"))
print(card_line(f"Hobby:      {hobby}"))

# Blank line for spacing
print(blank_line)

# Name stats section
print(card_line("Name Stats:"))
print(card_line(f"  Length:    {name_length} characters"))
print(card_line(f"  Uppercase: {name.upper()}"))
print(card_line(f"  Reversed:  {reversed_name}"))

# Blank line for spacing
print(blank_line)

# Divider before the personalized greeting
print(mid_border)

# Personalized greeting at the bottom
greeting = f"Keep {hobby.lower()}ing, {name.split()[0]}!"
print(card_line(f'"{greeting}"'))
print(card_line(f" You are doing great in {city}!"))

# Bottom border
print(bot_border)

# --- Bonus: print some fun facts ---
print(f"\nFun facts about {name.split()[0]}:")
print(f"  - Your username ({username}) has {len(username)} characters")
print(f"  - You've been alive for roughly {days_alive:,} days")
print(f"  - By your 100th birthday, you'll have lived ~{100 * 365:,} days")
print(f"  - You have {100 - age} more years until you turn 100!")
```

# Week 1: Variables & Data Types

**Motto**: "Every program starts with a value."

## Overview

Welcome to programming! This week you will learn the absolute basics, the building blocks that every single program is made of. Think of this week as learning the alphabet before you can write sentences. By the end, you will know how to store information, do math, work with text, and talk to the user. These skills are used in every Python program ever written, from simple scripts to massive applications.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this week, you will:
- Understand what a variable is and how to create one
- Know the four basic data types: integers, floats, strings, and booleans
- Display output to the screen with `print()`
- Ask the user for input with `input()`
- Convert between data types using `int()`, `float()`, `str()`, `bool()`
- Format text using f-strings
- Perform math operations in Python
- Manipulate strings (combine them, repeat them, measure them)
- Write comments to explain your code

## Core Concepts

### What is a Variable?

Imagine you have a bunch of labeled boxes. Each box has a name written on it, and inside the box you can put one thing. That is exactly what a variable is in Python, a name that holds a value.

```python
name = "Alice"       # A box labeled "name" containing the text "Alice"
age = 25             # A box labeled "age" containing the number 25
temperature = 98.6   # A box labeled "temperature" containing 98.6
is_sunny = True      # A box labeled "is_sunny" containing True
```

You choose the name. Python remembers the value. Later, you can look inside the box (use the variable) or change what is inside it.

**Rules for naming variables:**
- Must start with a letter or underscore (`_`)
- Can contain letters, numbers, and underscores
- No spaces allowed (use underscores instead: `my_name`, not `my name`)
- Case-sensitive (`Name` and `name` are different variables)
- Cannot use Python keywords (`if`, `for`, `while`, etc.)

### Data Types: The Four Basics

Every value in Python has a **type**. It tells Python what kind of data it is. Think of it like this: a box can hold a number, or a word, or a yes/no answer. Python needs to know which kind it is.

**`int`** (integer): Whole numbers, no decimal point.
```python
score = 100
negative = -5
zero = 0
```

**`float`** (floating-point): Numbers with a decimal point.
```python
price = 9.99
pi = 3.14159
half = 0.5
```

**`str`** (string): Text. Always wrapped in quotes (single or double).
```python
greeting = "Hello, World!"
letter = 'A'
empty = ""
```

**`bool`** (boolean): Only two possible values: `True` or `False`.
```python
is_raining = True
has_homework = False
```

You can check the type of any value using `type()`:
```python
print(type(42))        # <class 'int'>
print(type(3.14))      # <class 'float'>
print(type("hello"))   # <class 'str'>
print(type(True))      # <class 'bool'>
```

### print(): Showing Output

`print()` is how your program talks to the user. Whatever you put inside the parentheses gets displayed on the screen.

```python
print("Hello!")               # Prints: Hello!
print(42)                     # Prints: 42
print("Age:", 25)             # Prints: Age: 25  (comma adds a space)
print("Line 1\nLine 2")      # Prints on two lines (\n = new line)
```

### input(): Getting User Input

`input()` pauses the program and waits for the user to type something. Whatever they type comes back as a **string** (text), even if they type a number.

```python
name = input("What is your name? ")    # Asks the question, stores the answer
print("Hello,", name)

age_text = input("How old are you? ")  # This is a STRING, not a number!
age = int(age_text)                    # Convert the string to an integer
```

**Important:** `input()` always returns a string. If you need a number, you must convert it.

### Type Conversion

Sometimes you need to change a value from one type to another. Python gives you functions for this:

```python
# String to integer
age = int("25")           # "25" becomes 25

# String to float
price = float("9.99")    # "9.99" becomes 9.99

# Number to string
text = str(42)            # 42 becomes "42"

# Anything to boolean
bool(1)                   # True  (any non-zero number is True)
bool(0)                   # False (zero is False)
bool("hello")             # True  (any non-empty string is True)
bool("")                  # False (empty string is False)
```

### f-strings: Formatted Text

f-strings let you put variables directly inside text. Put an `f` before the opening quote, then use curly braces `{}` around variable names.

```python
name = "Alice"
age = 25
print(f"My name is {name} and I am {age} years old.")
# Output: My name is Alice and I am 25 years old.

# You can do math inside the braces too!
price = 9.99
quantity = 3
print(f"Total: ${price * quantity:.2f}")
# Output: Total: $29.97
```

### Math Operators

Python can do all the math you need:

| Operator | What it does        | Example      | Result  |
|----------|---------------------|--------------|---------|
| `+`      | Addition            | `5 + 3`      | `8`     |
| `-`      | Subtraction         | `10 - 4`     | `6`     |
| `*`      | Multiplication      | `7 * 3`      | `21`    |
| `/`      | Division            | `15 / 4`     | `3.75`  |
| `//`     | Floor division      | `15 // 4`    | `3`     |
| `%`      | Modulo (remainder)  | `15 % 4`     | `3`     |
| `**`     | Exponent (power)    | `2 ** 3`     | `8`     |

**Floor division** (`//`) divides and rounds down to the nearest whole number.
**Modulo** (`%`) gives you the remainder after division. Great for checking if a number is even (`number % 2 == 0`).

### String Operations

Strings have their own special operations:

```python
# Concatenation (joining strings together)
first = "Hello"
second = "World"
combined = first + " " + second    # "Hello World"

# Repetition (repeating a string)
line = "-" * 20                    # "--------------------"
echo = "ha" * 3                    # "hahaha"

# Length (counting characters)
message = "Hello"
print(len(message))                # 5

# Accessing characters (counting starts at 0!)
print(message[0])                  # "H"  (first character)
print(message[-1])                 # "o"  (last character)

# Useful string methods
text = "Hello World"
print(text.upper())                # "HELLO WORLD"
print(text.lower())                # "hello world"
print(text.replace("World", "Python"))  # "Hello Python"
```

### Comments

Comments are notes you write in your code for humans to read. Python ignores them completely.

```python
# This is a comment. Python skips this line
name = "Alice"  # You can also put comments at the end of a line

# Comments help you:
# 1. Explain WHY you did something
# 2. Leave notes for yourself or others
# 3. Temporarily disable code while testing
```

## Break-and-Fix Drills

### Drill 1: Type Mismatch
Try this code and see what happens:
```python
age = input("Enter your age: ")
next_year = age + 1
print(f"Next year you will be {next_year}")
```
It will crash! The `input()` function returns a string, and you cannot add a number to a string. Fix it by converting `age` to an integer: `age = int(input("Enter your age: "))`.

### Drill 2: String Concatenation Confusion
Try this code:
```python
name = "Alice"
age = 25
print("Hello, " + name + ". You are " + age + " years old.")
```
It will crash! You cannot concatenate (join) a string and an integer with `+`. Fix it by converting `age` to a string: `str(age)`, or better yet, use an f-string: `f"Hello, {name}. You are {age} years old."`.

## Exercises

Complete exercises 1-6 in the exercises.md file. These cover variables, data types, input/output, type conversion, f-strings, math, and string operations.

## Mini-Project

Build a Personal Profile Card that collects user information and displays it in a formatted card. See mini-project.md for full specifications.

## Daily Plan

- **Day 1**: Read this README thoroughly, try all the code examples in your Python interpreter, do Break-and-Fix drills
- **Day 2**: Complete Exercises 1-2 (variable types, mad libs)
- **Day 3**: Complete Exercises 3-4 (tip calculator, temperature converter)
- **Day 4**: Complete Exercises 5-6 (string explorer, quiz game), start the mini-project
- **Day 5**: Finish the mini-project, review your code against the rubric, study the provided solutions

## Key Takeaways

1. Variables are named containers that store values. You create them with `=` (the assignment operator).
2. Every value has a type (int, float, str, bool), and the type determines what you can do with it.
3. `print()` shows output; `input()` gets user input (always as a string).
4. Type conversion (`int()`, `float()`, `str()`) lets you change a value from one type to another, essential when working with user input.
5. f-strings are the easiest way to combine variables and text: `f"Hello, {name}!"`.
6. Python does math with `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, `%`, `**`, and follows the same order of operations you learned in school.

## Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+ installed on your computer
- A text editor or IDE (VS Code recommended for beginners)
- No prior programming experience required. This is Day 1!

## Resources

- Official Python tutorial (start here): https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/introduction.html
- Python string methods: https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#string-methods
- Python built-in functions: https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html
- f-string formatting: https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/inputoutput.html#formatted-string-literals

# Week 1: Assessment Rubric

## Pass/Fail Criteria

### PASS Requirements (All must be met)

#### Variables & Data Types
- [ ] Created variables of all four types: int, float, str, bool
- [ ] Used `type()` to check and display variable types
- [ ] Variable names follow Python conventions (snake_case, descriptive)
- [ ] Understands the difference between each data type

#### Input & Output
- [ ] Used `input()` to get information from the user
- [ ] Used `print()` to display results
- [ ] Prompt messages are clear and tell the user what to type
- [ ] Output is readable and well-labeled

#### Type Conversion
- [ ] Converted user input from string to int or float where needed
- [ ] Used `int()`, `float()`, `str()` correctly
- [ ] Understands that `input()` always returns a string
- [ ] No type errors from mixing strings and numbers

#### f-strings & Formatting
- [ ] Used f-strings (f"...{variable}...") for formatted output
- [ ] Formatted numbers to specific decimal places (e.g., `:.2f`)
- [ ] Combined variables and text smoothly in output
- [ ] Output is well-organized and easy to read

#### Math Operations
- [ ] Used at least 3 different math operators (+, -, *, /, //, %, **)
- [ ] Calculations produce correct results
- [ ] Understands the difference between `/` and `//`
- [ ] Used parentheses where needed to control order of operations

#### String Operations
- [ ] Used at least 3 string methods (.upper(), .lower(), .replace(), etc.)
- [ ] Used `len()` to measure string length
- [ ] Used string slicing (at least `[::-1]` for reversing)
- [ ] Used string concatenation (`+`) or repetition (`*`)

### Quality Checklist (Aim for 80%+)

#### Code Organization
- [ ] Code is organized in logical sections
- [ ] Related operations are grouped together
- [ ] No unnecessary or dead code
- [ ] Program flows from top to bottom in a logical order

#### Comments
- [ ] Comments explain WHY, not just WHAT
- [ ] Each major section has a comment explaining its purpose
- [ ] Comments are helpful for someone reading the code for the first time
- [ ] Not over-commented (no comment on every single line)

#### User Experience
- [ ] Prompts are clear and friendly
- [ ] Output is formatted cleanly with labels
- [ ] Results are easy to understand
- [ ] The program feels complete (has a beginning and end)

#### Robustness
- [ ] Program handles typical inputs without crashing
- [ ] Dollar amounts are formatted to 2 decimal places
- [ ] No obvious logical errors in calculations
- [ ] String operations handle spaces and mixed case

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

1. **Forgetting to convert input**: `input()` always returns a string. Writing `age = input("Age: ")` and then `age + 1` will crash. Fix: `age = int(input("Age: "))`.
2. **Using `+` to combine strings and numbers**: `"Age: " + 25` crashes. Use f-strings instead: `f"Age: {age}"`, or convert the number: `"Age: " + str(25)`.
3. **Integer division surprise**: `5 / 2` gives `2.5` (float), not `2`. If you want `2`, use `5 // 2` (floor division).
4. **Missing the `f` in f-strings**: Writing `"Hello {name}"` instead of `f"Hello {name}"`, without the `f`, the curly braces are treated as literal text.
5. **Confusing `=` and `==`**: `=` assigns a value (`x = 5`). `==` compares values (`x == 5` asks "is x equal to 5?"). We will cover `==` more in Week 2.
6. **Case sensitivity**: `Name` and `name` are two different variables. `"Hello" == "hello"` is `False`. Use `.lower()` when comparing text.
7. **Off-by-one in string indexing**: `name[1]` is the SECOND character, not the first. Python counting starts at 0.
8. **Not using `:` in format specs**: Writing `f"{price:2f}"` instead of `f"{price:.2f}"`, the dot before the number is required.
9. **Forgetting quotes around strings**: `name = Alice` crashes because Python thinks Alice is a variable. Fix: `name = "Alice"`.
10. **Modifying strings in place**: Strings are immutable. `name.upper()` returns a NEW string; it does not change `name`. You need `name = name.upper()`.

## Self-Assessment Questions

1. What is the difference between `int` and `float`? When would you use each?
2. Why does `input()` always return a string, and what do you do when you need a number?
3. What does `f` before a string literal do, and what goes inside the `{}`?
4. What is the difference between `/` and `//`? What does `%` do?
5. How do you reverse a string in Python? What does `[::-1]` mean?
6. If you write `x = "5"` and `y = 3`, what happens when you try `x + y`? How do you fix it?

## Grading Breakdown (if self-scoring)

- Variables and data types (all 4 types demonstrated): 15 points
- Input/output (input() and print() used correctly): 15 points
- Type conversion (string to int/float, correct usage): 15 points
- f-strings and formatting (clean, formatted output): 15 points
- Math operations (correct calculations, multiple operators): 15 points
- String operations (methods, slicing, len()): 15 points
- Code quality (comments, organization, readability): 10 points

**Total: 100 points**
**Passing score: 70 points**

# Week 6: Solutions

## Exercise 1 Solution: File Reader, Text File Analyzer

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Exercise 1 Solution: File Reader, Text File Analyzer
# ------------------------------------------------------------------


def create_sample_file(filename):
    """Create a sample text file for testing."""
    lines = [
        "Python is a versatile programming language.",
        "It was created by Guido van Rossum in 1991.",
        "Python emphasizes code readability.",
        "It supports multiple programming paradigms.",
        "Python has a large standard library.",
        "Many developers love Python for its simplicity.",
        "You can use Python for web development, data science, and more.",
        "The Python community is welcoming and helpful.",
    ]
    with open(filename, "w") as file:
        for line in lines:
            file.write(line + "\n")
    print(f"Created sample file: {filename}")


def count_lines(filename):
    """Count how many lines are in a file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the text file.

    Returns:
        The number of lines, or -1 if the file does not exist.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            lines = file.readlines()
            return len(lines)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File not found: {filename}")
        return -1


def count_words(filename):
    """Count the total number of words in a file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the text file.

    Returns:
        The word count, or -1 if the file does not exist.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            content = file.read()
            words = content.split()
            return len(words)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File not found: {filename}")
        return -1


def count_characters(filename):
    """Count characters in a file (total and non-whitespace).

    Args:
        filename: Path to the text file.

    Returns:
        A tuple: (total_chars, non_whitespace_chars), or (-1, -1) if not found.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            content = file.read()
            total = len(content)
            # Count non-whitespace: remove all spaces, tabs, newlines, then count
            non_whitespace = sum(1 for char in content if not char.isspace())
            return (total, non_whitespace)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File not found: {filename}")
        return (-1, -1)


def find_longest_line(filename):
    """Find the longest line in a file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the text file.

    Returns:
        A tuple: (line_number, line_text, length), or None if not found.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            longest_num = 0
            longest_text = ""
            longest_len = 0

            for i, line in enumerate(file, start=1):
                # Strip the newline for length comparison
                stripped = line.rstrip("\n")
                if len(stripped) > longest_len:
                    longest_num = i
                    longest_text = stripped
                    longest_len = len(stripped)

            return (longest_num, longest_text, longest_len)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File not found: {filename}")
        return None


def analyze_file(filename):
    """Print a complete analysis report for a text file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the text file.
    """
    print(f"\n--- File Analysis: {filename} ---")

    lines = count_lines(filename)
    if lines == -1:
        print("Cannot analyze: file not found.")
        return

    words = count_words(filename)
    total_chars, non_ws_chars = count_characters(filename)
    longest = find_longest_line(filename)

    print(f"Lines:          {lines}")
    print(f"Words:          {words}")
    print(f"Characters:     {total_chars} ({non_ws_chars} non-whitespace)")

    if longest is not None:
        line_num, line_text, line_len = longest
        print(f"Longest line:   Line {line_num} ({line_len} chars)")
        print(f'  "{line_text}"')


# --- Test ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
    create_sample_file("sample.txt")
    analyze_file("sample.txt")

    print()
    analyze_file("nonexistent.txt")  # Should handle gracefully
```

```python
    """Add a new entry to the diary file.

    so previous entries are preserved.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the diary file.
        text: The diary entry text.
    """
    now = datetime.datetime.now()
    timestamp = now.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

    with open(filename, "a") as file:
        file.write("---\n")
        file.write(f"Date: {timestamp}\n")
        file.write(text + "\n")

    print("Entry added!")


def read_entries(filename):
    """Read and display all diary entries.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the diary file.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            content = file.read()
            if content.strip() == "":
                print("Diary is empty.")
            else:
                print(f"\n--- All Diary Entries ---")
                print(content)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("No diary entries yet. Start writing!")


def count_entries(filename):
    """Count the number of diary entries.

    Counts separator lines ('---') to determine entry count.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the diary file.

    Returns:
        The number of entries.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            count = 0
            for line in file:
                if line.strip() == "---":
                    count += 1
            return count
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 0


def search_entries(filename, keyword):
    """Search diary entries for a keyword.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the diary file.
        keyword: The search term (case-insensitive).

    Returns:
        The number of matching entries.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            content = file.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("No diary entries to search.")
        return 0

    # Split into entries by the separator
    entries = content.split("---")
    matches = 0

    keyword_lower = keyword.lower()

    for entry in entries:
        entry = entry.strip()
        if entry == "":
            continue
        if keyword_lower in entry.lower():
            matches += 1
            print(f"\n--- Match #{matches} ---")
            print(entry)

    if matches == 0:
        print(f"No entries found containing '{keyword}'.")

    return matches


def run_diary():
    """Run the diary application with a menu-driven interface."""
    filename = "diary.txt"

    print("=" * 35)
    print("      MY DIARY")
    print("=" * 35)

    while True:
        print("\n--- Menu ---")
        print("1. Add entry")
        print("2. Read all entries")
        print("3. Count entries")
        print("4. Search entries")
        print("5. Quit")

        choice = input("\nChoose an option (1-5): ").strip()

        if choice == "1":
            print("\nWrite your diary entry (press Enter when done):")
            text = input("> ")
            if text.strip():
                add_entry(filename, text)
            else:
                print("Empty entry: nothing saved.")

        elif choice == "2":
            read_entries(filename)

        elif choice == "3":
            count = count_entries(filename)
            print(f"\nTotal entries: {count}")

        elif choice == "4":
            keyword = input("\nSearch for: ").strip()
            if keyword:
                matches = search_entries(filename, keyword)
                print(f"\nFound {matches} matching entry/entries.")
            else:
                print("Please enter a search term.")

        elif choice == "5":
            print("\nGoodbye! Keep writing!")
            break

        else:
            print("Invalid option. Please choose 1-5.")


# --- Test ---
if __name__ == "__main__":
```

```python
import csv

    ]

    with open(filename, "w", newline="") as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=["name", "math", "science", "english"])
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(students)

    print(f"Created sample CSV: {filename}")


def read_scores(filename):
    """Read student scores from a CSV file.

    Converts score strings to integers.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the CSV file.

    Returns:
        A list of dictionaries with name (str) and scores (int).
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            reader = csv.DictReader(file)
            students = []
            for row in reader:
                student = {
                    "name": row["name"],
                    "math": int(row["math"]),
                    "science": int(row["science"]),
                    "english": int(row["english"]),
                }
                students.append(student)
            return students
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"File not found: {filename}")
        return []
    except ValueError as e:
        print(f"Error reading scores: {e}")
        return []


def calculate_averages(students):
    """Add average and letter grade to each student.

    Args:
        students: List of student dictionaries.

    Returns:
        The updated list with 'average' and 'letter_grade' keys added.
    """
    for student in students:
        total = student["math"] + student["science"] + student["english"]
        average = round(total / 3, 1)
        student["average"] = average

        # Determine letter grade
        if average >= 90:
            student["letter_grade"] = "A"
        elif average >= 80:
            student["letter_grade"] = "B"
        elif average >= 70:
            student["letter_grade"] = "C"
        elif average >= 60:
            student["letter_grade"] = "D"
        else:
            student["letter_grade"] = "F"

    return students


def write_results(filename, students):
    """Write student results to a CSV file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the output CSV file.
        students: List of student dictionaries (with averages).
    """
    fieldnames = ["name", "math", "science", "english", "average", "letter_grade"]

    with open(filename, "w", newline="") as file:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(students)

    print(f"Results written to {filename}")

              f"{s['english']:>8} {s['average']:>8.1f} {s['letter_grade']:>6}")

              f"{avg_eng:>8.1f} {avg_overall:>8.1f}")


# --- Test ---
```

```python
import json


def create_default_config(filename):
    """Create a default settings file and return the config.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the JSON config file.

    Returns:
        The default configuration dictionary.
    """
    config = {

        "version": "1.0",
        "theme": "light",
        "font_size": 14,
        "auto_save": True,
        "recent_files": [],
        "window": {
            "width": 800,
            "height": 600,
            "x": 100,
            "y": 100,
        },
    }

    with open(filename, "w") as file:
        json.dump(config, file, indent=4)

    print(f"Created default config: {filename}")
    return config


def load_config(filename):
    """Load settings from a JSON file.

    If the file does not exist or is corrupted, create defaults.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the JSON config file.

    Returns:
        The configuration dictionary.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            config = json.load(file)
            print(f"Loaded settings from {filename}")
            return config
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"{filename} not found. Creating defaults...")
        return create_default_config(filename)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        print(f"{filename} is corrupted. Recreating defaults...")
        return create_default_config(filename)


def save_config(filename, config):
    """Save settings to a JSON file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the JSON config file.
        config: The configuration dictionary.
    """
    with open(filename, "w") as file:
        json.dump(config, file, indent=4)
    print("Settings saved.")


def update_setting(config, key, value):
    """Update a setting, supporting dot notation for nested keys.

    Examples:
        update_setting(config, "theme", "dark")
        update_setting(config, "window.width", 1024)

    Args:
        config: The configuration dictionary.
        key: The setting key (supports "parent.child" dot notation).
        value: The new value.

    Returns:
        True if successful.
    """
    parts = key.split(".")

    # Navigate to the correct nested level
    current = config
    for part in parts[:-1]:  # All parts except the last one
        if part in current and isinstance(current[part], dict):
            current = current[part]
        else:
            print(f"Setting path '{key}' not found.")
            return False

    # Set the final key
    last_key = parts[-1]
    old_value = current.get(last_key, "<new>")
    current[last_key] = value
    print(f"Updated: {key} = {value} (was: {old_value})")
    return True


def display_config(config, indent=0):
    """Display all settings in a readable format.

    Handles nested dictionaries and lists.

    Args:
        config: The configuration dictionary.
        indent: Current indentation level (for recursion).
    """
    prefix = "  " * indent

    for key, value in config.items():
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            print(f"{prefix}{key}:")
            display_config(value, indent + 1)
        elif isinstance(value, list):
            if len(value) == 0:
                print(f"{prefix}{key}: (empty)")
            else:
                print(f"{prefix}{key}:")
                for item in value:
                    print(f"{prefix}  - {item}")
        else:
            print(f"{prefix}{key}: {value}")


def run_settings_manager():
    """Run the settings manager with a menu-driven interface."""
    filename = "settings.json"
    config = load_config(filename)
    changed = False

    print("\n" + "=" * 35)
    print("    SETTINGS MANAGER")
    print("=" * 35)

    while True:
        print("\n--- Menu ---")
        print("1. View settings")
        print("2. Change a setting")
        print("3. Reset to defaults")
        print("4. Save settings")
        print("5. Quit")

        choice = input("\nChoose an option (1-5): ").strip()

        if choice == "1":
            print("\n--- Current Settings ---")
            display_config(config)

        elif choice == "2":
            key = input("Setting name (e.g., 'theme' or 'window.width'): ").strip()
            value_str = input("New value: ").strip()

            # Try to convert to appropriate type
            # Try int first, then float, then bool, then keep as string
            try:
                value = int(value_str)
            except ValueError:
                try:
                    value = float(value_str)
                except ValueError:
                    if value_str.lower() == "true":
                        value = True
                    elif value_str.lower() == "false":
                        value = False
                    else:
                        value = value_str

            if update_setting(config, key, value):
                changed = True

        elif choice == "3":
            config = create_default_config(filename)
            changed = False
            print("Settings reset to defaults.")

        elif choice == "4":
            save_config(filename, config)
            changed = False

        elif choice == "5":
            if changed:
                save_choice = input("You have unsaved changes. Save? (yes/no): ").strip().lower()
                if save_choice in ["yes", "y"]:
                    save_config(filename, config)
            print("Goodbye!")
            break

        else:
            print("Invalid option. Please choose 1-5.")


# --- Test ---
```

```python
def safe_divide(a, b):
    """Safely divide two numbers, handling errors.

    Args:
        a: The dividend (numerator).
        b: The divisor (denominator).

    Returns:
        The result of a / b, or None if an error occurs.
    """
    try:
        result = a / b
        return result
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("Error: Cannot divide by zero.")
        return None
    except TypeError:
        print(f"Error: Cannot divide {type(a).__name__} by {type(b).__name__}.")
        return None


def safe_int(value, default=0):
    """Safely convert a value to an integer.

    Args:
        value: The value to convert.
        default: What to return if conversion fails (default 0).

    Returns:
        The integer value, or default if conversion fails.
    """
    try:
        return int(value)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return default


def safe_list_access(my_list, index, default=None):
    """Safely access a list item by index.

    Args:
        my_list: The list to access.
        index: The index to look up.
        default: What to return if access fails (default None).

    Returns:
        The item at the index, or default if access fails.
    """
    try:
        return my_list[index]
    except (IndexError, TypeError):
        return default


def safe_dict_access(my_dict, key, default=None):
    """Safely access a dictionary value by key.

    Args:
        my_dict: The dictionary to access.
        key: The key to look up.
        default: What to return if access fails (default None).

    Returns:
        The value for the key, or default if access fails.
    """
    try:
        return my_dict[key]
    except (KeyError, TypeError):
        return default


def safe_file_read(filename, default=""):
    """Safely read the entire contents of a file.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the file.
        default: What to return if reading fails (default "").

    Returns:
        The file contents as a string, or default if reading fails.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            return file.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return default
    except PermissionError:
        print(f"Error: No permission to read {filename}.")
        return default
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Unexpected error reading {filename}: {e}")
        return default


def validate_input(prompt, validator_func, error_message):
    """Get validated input from the user.

    Keeps asking until the validator function returns True.

    Args:
        prompt: The input prompt to display.
        validator_func: A function that takes a string and returns True/False.
        error_message: What to display when validation fails.

    Returns:
        The validated input string.
    """
    while True:
        user_input = input(prompt)
        try:
            if validator_func(user_input):
                return user_input
            else:
                print(error_message)
        except Exception:
            print(error_message)
```

```python
import datetime
import time


def format_currency(amount):
    """Format a number as currency with dollar sign and commas.

    Args:
        amount: A number to format.

    Returns:
        A formatted string like "$1,234.56".
    """
    return f"${amount:,.2f}"


def format_date(date_obj=None):
    """Format a datetime object as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

    Args:
        date_obj: A datetime object (defaults to now if None).

    Returns:
        A formatted date string.
    """
    if date_obj is None:
        date_obj = datetime.datetime.now()
    return date_obj.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def validate_email(email):
    """Check if a string looks like a valid email address.

    Basic check: must contain @ and a . after the @.

    Args:
        email: The email string to validate.

    Returns:
        True if it looks valid, False otherwise.
    """
    if "@" not in email:
        return False
    parts = email.split("@")
    if len(parts) != 2:
        return False
    if "." not in parts[1]:
        return False
    if len(parts[0]) == 0 or len(parts[1]) < 3:
        return False
    return True


def truncate_string(text, max_length=50):
    """Shorten a string and add '...' if it exceeds max_length.

    Args:
        text: The string to truncate.
        max_length: Maximum allowed length (default 50).

    Returns:
        The original string if short enough, or truncated with '...'.
    """
    if len(text) <= max_length:
        return text
    return text[:max_length - 3] + "..."


def generate_id():
    """Generate a simple unique ID based on the current timestamp.

    Returns:
        A string ID like "1705123456789".
    """
    return str(int(time.time() * 1000))
```

## Mini-Project Solution: Contact Manager

```python
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mini-Project Solution: Contact Manager
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# A complete contact management application that saves to JSON,
# exports to CSV, and uses all concepts from Weeks 1-6.
#
# This is the capstone project for CODE Skool.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------

import json
import csv


# =====================================================================
# FILE I/O FUNCTIONS
# =====================================================================

def load_contacts(filename="contacts.json"):
    """Load contacts from a JSON file.

    If the file does not exist or is corrupted, return an empty list.

    Args:
        filename: Path to the JSON file.

    Returns:
        A list of contact dictionaries.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "r") as file:
            contacts = json.load(file)
            print(f"Loaded {len(contacts)} contact(s).")
            return contacts
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("No existing contacts file. Starting fresh.")
        return []
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        print("Warning: Contacts file is corrupted. Starting fresh.")
        return []


def save_contacts(contacts, filename="contacts.json"):
    """Save all contacts to a JSON file.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        filename: Path to the JSON file.
    """
    try:
        with open(filename, "w") as file:
            json.dump(contacts, file, indent=4)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error saving contacts: {e}")


def export_to_csv(contacts, filename="contacts.csv"):
    """Export all contacts to a CSV file.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        filename: Path to the CSV file.
    """
    if len(contacts) == 0:
        print("No contacts to export.")
        return

    fieldnames = ["id", "name", "phone", "email", "category"]

    try:
        with open(filename, "w", newline="") as file:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=fieldnames)
            writer.writeheader()
            writer.writerows(contacts)
        print(f"Contacts exported to {filename} ({len(contacts)} contacts)")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error exporting to CSV: {e}")


# =====================================================================
# CONTACT MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# =====================================================================

def get_next_id(contacts):
    """Get the next available contact ID.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.

    Returns:
        The next available integer ID.
    """
    if len(contacts) == 0:
        return 1
    return max(contact["id"] for contact in contacts) + 1


def add_contact(contacts):
    """Add a new contact by prompting the user for details.

    Validates that name is not empty and email contains '@'.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.

    Returns:
        The new contact dictionary, or None if cancelled.
    """
    print("\n--- Add New Contact ---")

    # Get name (required)
    name = input("Name: ").strip()
    if name == "":
        print("Name cannot be empty. Contact not added.")
        return None

    # Get phone
    phone = input("Phone: ").strip()

    # Get email (basic validation)
    email = input("Email: ").strip()
    if email != "" and "@" not in email:
        print("Warning: Email does not contain '@'. Adding anyway.")

    # Get category
    category = input("Category (friend/work/family/other): ").strip().lower()
    if category not in ["friend", "work", "family", "other"]:
        category = "other"

    # Create the contact
    contact = {
        "id": get_next_id(contacts),
        "name": name,
        "phone": phone,
        "email": email,
        "category": category,
    }

    contacts.append(contact)
    print(f"\nContact added: {name} (#{contact['id']})")
    return contact


def search_contacts(contacts, keyword):
    """Search contacts by name or category (case-insensitive).

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        keyword: The search term.

    Returns:
        A list of matching contact dictionaries.
    """
    keyword_lower = keyword.lower()
    results = []

    for contact in contacts:
        if (keyword_lower in contact["name"].lower() or
                keyword_lower in contact["category"].lower()):
            results.append(contact)

    return results


def find_contact_by_id(contacts, contact_id):
    """Find a contact by its ID.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        contact_id: The ID to search for.

    Returns:
        The contact dictionary, or None if not found.
    """
    for contact in contacts:
        if contact["id"] == contact_id:
            return contact
    return None


def edit_contact(contacts, contact_id):
    """Edit an existing contact.

    Shows current values and lets the user type new ones.
    Pressing Enter keeps the current value.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        contact_id: The ID of the contact to edit.

    Returns:
        True if edited, False if not found.
    """
    contact = find_contact_by_id(contacts, contact_id)
    if contact is None:
        print(f"Contact #{contact_id} not found.")
        return False

    print(f"\n--- Editing: {contact['name']} ---")
    print("(Press Enter to keep current value)")

    # Edit each field
    new_name = input(f"Name [{contact['name']}]: ").strip()
    if new_name != "":
        contact["name"] = new_name

    new_phone = input(f"Phone [{contact['phone']}]: ").strip()
    if new_phone != "":
        contact["phone"] = new_phone

    new_email = input(f"Email [{contact['email']}]: ").strip()
    if new_email != "":
        contact["email"] = new_email

    new_category = input(f"Category [{contact['category']}]: ").strip().lower()
    if new_category != "":
        contact["category"] = new_category

    print("\nContact updated!")
    return True


def delete_contact(contacts, contact_id):
    """Delete a contact by ID after confirmation.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        contact_id: The ID of the contact to delete.

    Returns:
        True if deleted, False if not found or cancelled.
    """
    contact = find_contact_by_id(contacts, contact_id)
    if contact is None:
        print(f"Contact #{contact_id} not found.")
        return False

    # Confirm deletion
    print(f"\nAbout to delete: {contact['name']} (#{contact['id']})")
    confirm = input("Are you sure? (yes/no): ").strip().lower()

    if confirm in ["yes", "y"]:
        contacts.remove(contact)
        print(f"Deleted: {contact['name']}")
        return True
    else:
        print("Deletion cancelled.")
        return False


# =====================================================================
# DISPLAY FUNCTIONS
# =====================================================================

def display_contacts(contacts, title="All Contacts"):
    """Display contacts in a formatted table.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
        title: The table header title.
    """
    if len(contacts) == 0:
        print(f"\n--- {title} ---")
        print("  No contacts to display.")
        return

    print(f"\n--- {title} ---")
    print(f" {'ID':>3} | {'Name':<18} | {'Phone':<13} | {'Email':<22} | {'Category'}")
    print(f"{'-----':>5}|{'--------------------':<20}|{'---------------':<15}|{'------------------------':<24}|{'----------'}")

    for c in contacts:
        print(f" {c['id']:>3} | {c['name']:<18} | {c['phone']:<13} | {c['email']:<22} | {c['category']}")


def display_categories(contacts):
    """Show categories and the number of contacts in each.

    Args:
        contacts: The list of contact dictionaries.
    """
    if len(contacts) == 0:
        print("\nNo contacts to categorize.")
        return

    # Count contacts per category
    categories = {}
    for contact in contacts:
        cat = contact["category"]
        if cat in categories:
            categories[cat] += 1
        else:
            categories[cat] = 1

    print("\n--- Contacts by Category ---")
    for category, count in sorted(categories.items()):
        print(f"  {category:<10}: {count} contact(s)")


# =====================================================================
# MENU AND MAIN LOOP
# =====================================================================

def show_menu():
    """Display the main menu."""
    print("\n--- Menu ---")
    print("1. Add contact")
    print("2. Search contacts")
    print("3. Edit contact")
    print("4. Delete contact")
    print("5. Display all contacts")
    print("6. Display by category")
    print("7. Export to CSV")
    print("8. Quit")


def get_valid_id(prompt):
    """Get a valid integer ID from the user.

    Args:
        prompt: The prompt to display.

    Returns:
        An integer ID.
    """
    while True:
        user_input = input(prompt).strip()
        try:
            return int(user_input)
        except ValueError:
            print("  Please enter a valid number.")


def main():
    """Main program loop.

    Loads contacts on startup, shows a menu, processes choices,
    and auto-saves after changes.
    """
    filename = "contacts.json"

    print("=" * 42)
    print("        CONTACT MANAGER")
    print("=" * 42)

    # Load contacts on startup
    contacts = load_contacts(filename)

    while True:
        show_menu()
        choice = input("\nChoose an option (1-8): ").strip()

        if choice == "1":
            # Add contact
            result = add_contact(contacts)
            if result is not None:
                save_contacts(contacts, filename)
                print("Contacts saved.")

        elif choice == "2":
            # Search
            keyword = input("\nEnter search term: ").strip()
            if keyword == "":
                print("Please enter a search term.")
                continue
            results = search_contacts(contacts, keyword)
            if len(results) == 0:
                print(f"No contacts found matching '{keyword}'.")
            else:
                display_contacts(results, f'Search Results for "{keyword}"')

        elif choice == "3":
            # Edit
            if len(contacts) == 0:
                print("\nNo contacts to edit.")
                continue
            display_contacts(contacts)
            contact_id = get_valid_id("\nEnter contact ID to edit: ")
            if edit_contact(contacts, contact_id):
                save_contacts(contacts, filename)
                print("Contacts saved.")

        elif choice == "4":
            # Delete
            if len(contacts) == 0:
                print("\nNo contacts to delete.")
                continue
            display_contacts(contacts)
            contact_id = get_valid_id("\nEnter contact ID to delete: ")
            if delete_contact(contacts, contact_id):
                save_contacts(contacts, filename)
                print("Contacts saved.")

        elif choice == "5":
            # Display all
            display_contacts(contacts)

        elif choice == "6":
            # Display by category
            display_categories(contacts)

        elif choice == "7":
            # Export to CSV
            export_to_csv(contacts)

        elif choice == "8":
            # Quit
            save_contacts(contacts, filename)
            print(f"\nContacts saved. Goodbye!")
            break

        else:
            print("Invalid option. Please choose 1-8.")


# Start the program
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```
